### CLAUDE (2026-07-30T15:35:51.023Z)

To run this Next.js app you need three things:

1. **Node.js** — the README says 18+, but Next.js 16 actually requires Node 20.9 or newer, so use Node 20+.
2. **Dependencies installed** — run `npm install` in the project root (there's no `node_modules` or lockfile yet).
3. **A NextBillion.ai API key** — copy `.env.example` (the file you have open) to `.env.local` and fill in both variables with your key from nextbillion.ai:
   - `NEXTBILLION_API_KEY` — used server-side by the API proxy routes
   - `NEXT_PUBLIC_NEXTBILLION_API_KEY` — used client-side for map rendering

Then start it with:

```bash
npm run dev
```

and open http://localhost:3000. Despite the folder name (`tomtom_playground`), the app is a NextBillion.ai routing playground — no TomTom key is needed.

### CLAUDE (2026-07-30T15:38:41.480Z)

Fixed — the app now installs and runs. `npm run dev` from the project directory serves http://localhost:3000 with HTTP 200 (I started it, verified, and stopped it again).

Three things were in the way:

1. **The failed `npm install` ran in the wrong directory.** After your two `cd ..` you were in `~/workspace`, which has its own unrelated `package.json` — that's whose dependency conflict you hit. (I left that directory untouched.)
2. **A real dependency conflict in this project too**: `package.json` pinned `redux@^4.2.1`, but `react-redux@9` requires redux 5. I bumped it to `redux@^5.0.1` (compatible with `@rematch/core`) and ran `npm install` successfully — 489 packages added.
3. **Next.js 16 refused to start** because the config only had a `webpack` customization while Turbopack is now the default bundler. I added the equivalent `turbopack.resolveAlias` (`mapbox-gl` → `maplibre-gl`) plus `turbopack.root` so it stops mis-detecting `~/workspace` as the project root.

One thing left for you: there's no `.env.local` yet, so the server runs but map rendering and routing calls will fail until you create it:

```bash
cd ~/workspace/tomtom_playground
cp .env.example .env.local   # then paste your NextBillion.ai key into both variables
npm run dev
```

Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

### CLAUDE (2026-08-20T14:58:30.638Z)

All three behaviors now work, and it took a one-line fix. The feature was already fully implemented in the codebase (markers in `WaypointMarkers.tsx`, drag handling in `useMapInteraction.ts`, auto-recalculation in `useRouting.ts`) — but it was invisible because `maplibre-gl`'s stylesheet was never imported. Without it, `.maplibregl-marker` elements have no `position: absolute`, so the pins were rendering as full-width blocks *below* the map instead of on it. The fix was adding to `src/components/map/MapContainer.tsx:8`:

```ts
import 'maplibre-gl/dist/maplibre-gl.css';
```

I verified everything live in Chrome against your running dev server (it's on **http://localhost:3001** — port 3000 is occupied by your AUTO_CARRIER demo):

- **First click** places the green "A" origin pin; **second click** places the red "B" destination pin, and a route immediately draws between them (Amsterdam → Cologne, 346 km / 3h 58min).
- **Dragging a marker** updates its coordinates in the sidebar and recalculates the route — I dragged B to Frankfurt and the route redrew at 500 km / 5h 22min. Recalculation is debounced 500 ms, so it fires once on drop rather than during the drag.
- **A third click** adds a numbered intermediate waypoint (I added one near Brussels) and the route reroutes through it.

The navigation zoom controls in the bottom-right corner were also casualties of the missing CSS and now show up correctly. I left the browser tab open so you can try it yourself.

{
 "file_path": "/Users/[USER]/workspace/tomtom_playground/src/app/api/geocoding/reverse/route.ts",
 "content": "/**\n * API Route: Proxy to NextBillion.ai Reverse Geocoding API\n * Protects API key and handles CORS\n */\nimport { NextRequest, NextResponse } from 'next/server';\n\nconst NB_API_KEY = process.env.NEXTBILLION_API_KEY || '';\nconst NB_API_BASE = 'https://api.nextbillion.io';\n\nexport async function GET(request: NextRequest) {\n  // Check API key\n  if (!NB_API_KEY) {\n    return NextResponse.json(\n      { status: 'Error', msg: 'API key not configured' },\n      { status: 500 }\n    );\n  }\n\n  const at = request.nextUrl.searchParams.get('at');\n  if (!at) {\n    return NextResponse.json(\n      { status: 'Error', msg: 'Missing \"at\" parameter (lat,lng)' },\n      { status: 400 }\n    );\n  }\n\n  const url = `${NB_API_BASE}/revgeocode?at=${encodeURIComponent(at)}&key=${NB_API_KEY}`;\n\n  try {\n    const response = await fetch(url, {\n      headers: {\n        'Accept': 'application/json',\n      },\n    });\n\n    const data = await response.json();\n\n    return NextResponse.json(data, {\n      status: response.status,\n      headers: {\n        'Cache-Control': 'no-store, max-age=0',\n      },\n    });\n  } catch (error) {\n    console.error('Reverse geocoding API error:', error);\n    return NextResponse.json(\n      { status: 'Error', msg: 'Failed to reverse geocode' },\n      { status: 500 }\n    );\n  }\n}\n"
}
```

 "content": "/**\n * NextBillion.ai Reverse Geocoding API Client\n */\n\nconst API_ENDPOINT = '/api/geocoding/reverse';\n\ninterface RevGeocodeResponse {\n  items?: Array<{\n    title?: string;\n    address?: { label?: string };\n  }>;\n}\n\n/**\n * Reverse geocodes coordinates into a human-readable address.\n * Returns null if no address is found or the request fails.\n */\nexport async function reverseGeocode(\n  coordinates: [number, number] // [lng, lat]\n): Promise<string | null> {\n  const [lng, lat] = coordinates;\n  const url = `${API_ENDPOINT}?at=${lat},${lng}`;\n\n  try {\n    const response = await fetch(url);\n    if (!response.ok) {\n      return null;\n    }\n\n    const data: RevGeocodeResponse = await response.json();\n    const item = data.items?.[0];\n    return item?.title || item?.address?.label || null;\n  } catch {\n    return null;\n  }\n}\n"
}

 "content": "/**\n * Custom hook that fills in waypoint names via reverse geocoding.\n * Watches all waypoints and resolves an address for any that lack a name\n * (newly added, or cleared after being repositioned).\n */\n'use client';\n\nimport { useEffect, useRef } from 'react';\nimport { useAppDispatch, useAppSelector } from '@/store/hooks';\nimport { reverseGeocode } from '@/services/geocoding/geocodingApi';\nimport type { Waypoint } from '@/types/routing';\n\nexport function useReverseGeocode() {\n  const dispatch = useAppDispatch();\n\n  const origin = useAppSelector((state) => state.waypoints.origin);\n  const destination = useAppSelector((state) => state.waypoints.destination);\n  const intermediates = useAppSelector((state) => state.waypoints.intermediates);\n\n  // Tracks id+coordinates already requested, so failures don't retry forever\n  const requestedRef = useRef<Set<string>>(new Set());\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    const pending: Waypoint[] = [origin, destination, ...intermediates].filter(\n      (wp): wp is Waypoint => !!wp && !wp.name\n    );\n\n    for (const waypoint of pending) {\n      const key = `${waypoint.id}|${waypoint.coordinates[0]},${waypoint.coordinates[1]}`;\n      if (requestedRef.current.has(key)) continue;\n      requestedRef.current.add(key);\n\n      reverseGeocode(waypoint.coordinates).then((name) => {\n        if (name) {\n          dispatch.waypoints.updateWaypoint({ id: waypoint.id, name });\n        }\n      });\n    }\n  }, [origin, destination, intermediates, dispatch]);\n}\n"
}

### CLAUDE (2026-08-20T15:06:32.107Z)

Both bugs are fixed and verified in the browser.

**NaN route legs** — the client parsed `leg.distance` as a plain number, but the Directions API actually returns legs as `{distance: {value: 233547}, duration: {value: 11276}}` (nested objects; only the route-level totals are flat numbers). I confirmed this by calling the API directly, then fixed the parsing in `src/services/routing/directionsApi.ts` with an unwrap helper that accepts both shapes, and corrected the `NBRouteLeg` type in `src/types/routing.ts`. The panel now shows real values ("Leg 1: 212 km, Leg 2: 264 km", summing to the 476 km total).

**"Unknown location"** — there was no reverse geocoding in the app at all; waypoint names were simply never populated. I added the full path:

- `src/app/api/geocoding/reverse/route.ts` — server proxy to NextBillion's `revgeocode` endpoint, keeping the API key server-side like the directions proxy.
- `src/services/geocoding/geocodingApi.ts` — small client that returns the address from `items[0].title`.
- `src/hooks/useReverseGeocode.ts` — mounted in `page.tsx`; watches all waypoints and resolves an address for any that lack a name, with a guard so failed lookups don't retry in a loop.
- In the waypoints store, moving a waypoint now clears its stale name, so a drag triggers a fresh lookup — verified: dragging B near Würzburg updated it to "97840 Fürstlich Löw…".

One knock-on issue I prevented: the route-recalculation effect keyed on waypoint object identity, so the name updates landing in the store would have re-fired route requests. `useRouting.ts` now keys on coordinates only.

The sidebar now shows proper addresses like "Karekietweg, 3898 Z…" for clicks, and even names ferry corridors ("Zeebrugge - Göteborg") when you click in the sea. One heads-up: if your browser tab shows a full-screen React error after these edits, it's a one-time Fast Refresh artifact (the hook's dependency array changed shape mid-session) — a normal reload clears it.

 "content": "/**\n * Traffic Toggle Control - native maplibre control so it stacks and aligns\n * with the navigation control in the map's control corner\n */\n'use client';\n\nimport { useEffect, useRef } from 'react';\nimport { useControl } from 'react-map-gl';\nimport type { IControl } from 'maplibre-gl';\n\n// Material Design \"Traffic\" icon, drawn with currentColor\nconst TRAFFIC_ICON_SVG = `\n<svg xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/2000/svg\" width=\"20\" height=\"20\" viewBox=\"0 0 24 24\" fill=\"currentColor\" style=\"display:block\">\n  <path d=\"M20 10h-3V8.86c1.72-.45 3-2 3-3.86h-3V4c0-.55-.45-1-1-1H8c-.55 0-1 .45-1 1v1H4c0 1.86 1.28 3.41 3 3.86V10H4c0 1.86 1.28 3.41 3 3.86V15H4c0 1.86 1.28 3.41 3 3.86V20c0 .55.45 1 1 1h8c.55 0 1-.45 1-1v-1.14c1.72-.45 3-2 3-3.86h-3v-1.14c1.72-.45 3-2 3-3.86zm-8 9c-1.11 0-2-.9-2-2s.89-2 2-2c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2s-.89 2-2 2zm0-5c-1.11 0-2-.9-2-2s.89-2 2-2c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2s-.89 2-2 2zm0-5c-1.11 0-2-.9-2-2 0-1.11.89-2 2-2 1.1 0 2 .89 2 2 0 1.1-.89 2-2 2z\"/>\n</svg>`;\n\nclass TrafficToggleControl implements IControl {\n  private container: HTMLDivElement | null = null;\n  private button: HTMLButtonElement | null = null;\n\n  constructor(private onClick: () => void) {}\n\n  onAdd(): HTMLElement {\n    this.container = document.createElement('div');\n    this.container.className = 'maplibregl-ctrl maplibregl-ctrl-group';\n\n    this.button = document.createElement('button');\n    this.button.type = 'button';\n    this.button.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Toggle traffic');\n    this.button.style.display = 'flex';\n    this.button.style.alignItems = 'center';\n    this.button.style.justifyContent = 'center';\n    this.button.addEventListener('click', () => this.onClick());\n    this.button.innerHTML = TRAFFIC_ICON_SVG;\n\n    this.container.appendChild(this.button);\n    return this.container;\n  }\n\n  onRemove(): void {\n    this.container?.remove();\n    this.container = null;\n    this.button = null;\n  }\n\n  setEnabled(enabled: boolean): void {\n    if (!this.button) return;\n    this.button.title = enabled ? 'Hide traffic' : 'Show traffic';\n    this.button.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(enabled));\n    this.button.style.color = enabled ? '#1976D2' : '#616161';\n  }\n}\n\ninterface TrafficControlProps {\n  enabled: boolean;\n  onToggle: () => void;\n}\n\nexport function TrafficControl({ enabled, onToggle }: TrafficControlProps) {\n  // Keep the latest callback without recreating the control\n  const onToggleRef = useRef(onToggle);\n  onToggleRef.current = onToggle;\n\n  const control = useControl<TrafficToggleControl>(\n    () => new TrafficToggleControl(() => onToggleRef.current()),\n    { position: 'top-right' }\n  );\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    control.setEnabled(enabled);\n  }, [control, enabled]);\n\n  return null;\n}\n\nexport default TrafficControl;\n"
}

That means it renders inside the same control corner as the zoom stack, using maplibre's own `ctrl-group` styling — identical 29px width, same right edge, same corner radius and shadow, and the standard 10px gap between groups. No magic pixel offsets to drift out of alignment if controls are added or the layout changes.

Verified in the browser: the button lines up flush with the navigation control, and toggling still works — the icon goes blue and the traffic style loads.

 "content": "# Deploying to Cloud Run\n\nOne-time bootstrap, then repeatable deploys. Requires `gcloud`, `docker`,\nand `terraform` >= 1.5, authenticated against your project\n(`gcloud auth login && gcloud auth application-default login`).\n\nAll configuration — GCP project, API key, region, sizing — lives in\nTerraform variables. Copy the example and fill it in:\n\n```bash\ncd terraform\ncp terraform.tfvars.example terraform.tfvars   # gitignored\nterraform init\n```\n\n> The API key is written to Secret Manager by Terraform, which means it\n> also lives in Terraform state. Keep state private (or use a GCS\n> backend with restricted access).\n\n## 1. Create the image repo\n\nThe Cloud Run service can't be created until an image exists, so create\nthe Artifact Registry repo first:\n\n```bash\nterraform apply -target=google_artifact_registry_repository.app\n```\n\n## 2. Build and push the image\n\nThe public map key is inlined into the client bundle at build time, so\nit must be passed as a Docker build arg (the server-side key is injected\nat runtime from Secret Manager and is NOT baked into the image):\n\n```bash\nREGION=us-central1\nREPO=$(terraform output -raw artifact_registry_repo)\nTAG=\"$REPO/routing-playground:$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)\"\nNB_KEY=$(grep '^NEXT_PUBLIC_NEXTBILLION_API_KEY=' ../.env.local | cut -d= -f2)\n\ngcloud auth configure-docker \"$REGION-docker.pkg.dev\"\ndocker build --platform linux/amd64 \\\n  --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_NEXTBILLION_API_KEY=\"$NB_KEY\" \\\n  -t \"$TAG\" ..\ndocker push \"$TAG\"\n```\n\n## 3. Deploy everything\n\n```bash\nterraform apply -var image=\"$TAG\"\n```\n\nThe service URL is in the `service_url` output.\n\n## Subsequent deploys\n\nRepeat steps 2–3 with a new tag (add `image` to `terraform.tfvars` if\nyou prefer not to pass it on the CLI). To rotate the API key, change\n`nextbillion_api_key` in `terraform.tfvars` and `terraform apply` — the\nservice pins the exact secret version, so a rotation automatically rolls\nout a new revision. (Rotating the public map key additionally requires\nrebuilding the image, since it is baked into the client bundle.)\n"
}
```

### CLAUDE (2026-08-20T17:54:32.595Z)

[tool: Bash — Patch rematch types for redux 5 compatibility]
```bash
python3 - <<'EOF'
import re
p = 'node_modules/@rematch/core/dist/types.d.ts'
src = open(p).read()

# Import UnknownAction alongside the other redux type imports
src = src.replace(
    "import { Action as ReduxAction, Reducer as ReduxReducer,",
    "import { UnknownAction, Action as ReduxAction, Reducer as ReduxReducer,",
    1)

# Match redux 5's Dispatch type parameters exactly
src = src.replace(
    "interface Dispatch<A extends Action = AnyAction> {",
    "interface Dispatch<A extends Action = UnknownAction> {",
    1)

# Remove the react-redux `connect` augmentation (references types that are
# never imported; broken against react-redux 9)
src = re.sub(r"declare module 'react-redux' \{.*?\n\}\n", "", src, flags=re.S)

open(p, 'w').write(src)
print("patched")
EOF
grep -n "UnknownAction\|react-redux" node_modules/@rematch/core/dist/types.d.ts | head
```

### CLAUDE (2026-08-20T18:02:18.656Z)

The Docker build is running in the background (it'll notify me when done). Current state of the deployment setup while it finishes:

**Created:**
- `Dockerfile` — multi-stage Node 20 Alpine build using Next.js standalone output (added `output: 'standalone'` to `next.config.js`), non-root runtime user, port 3000. The public map key is a build arg (`NEXT_PUBLIC_*` values are baked into the client bundle); the server key is injected at runtime and never enters the image.
- `terraform/` — `main.tf`, `variables.tf`, `outputs.tf`, `terraform.tfvars.example`, `README.md`, mirroring the territory-planner pattern: enables the run/artifactregistry/secretmanager APIs, an Artifact Registry repo, the server API key in Secret Manager (version-pinned so key rotation rolls a new revision), a dedicated runtime service account with `secretAccessor`, a Cloud Run v2 service named **routing-playground** (1 CPU / 512Mi, scale 0–2, public), and the service URL as an output. `terraform init && terraform validate && terraform fmt -check` all pass.
- `.dockerignore` and `.gitignore` (the repo had none — now tfvars/state, `.env.local`, `node_modules`, `.next` are excluded).

**Fixed along the way** — `npm run build` had never been run and failed type-checking (dev mode doesn't type-check). Three causes, all fixed and verified:
1. All Rematch dispatchers typed as `never`: the models passed a `selectors` block that `createModel` doesn't accept (it's from the uninstalled `@rematch/select` plugin — dead code at runtime too) which broke generic inference, plus missing `effects` anchors. Removed the selectors, added `effects: {}` to each model, gave zero-arg reducers a `_state` param.
2. `@rematch/core`'s bundled types augment redux with pre-v5 signatures — patched via `patch-package` (`patches/` + `postinstall` script, and the Dockerfile copies `patches/` before `npm ci`).
3. Small real errors: untyped `mapboxgl` namespace reference in `MapContainer`, missing `source` on the `RouteLayer` layer specs.

`npx tsc --noEmit` is clean, `npm run build` succeeds, and I re-verified the running app in the browser afterwards — markers, geocoded addresses, and routing all still work. I'll report the Docker build result when it lands.

### CLAUDE (2026-08-20T18:06:14.256Z)

Everything is validated. The clean key (no comment tail) is baked into the client bundle, and the deployment setup is complete.

**What you got:**

- **`Dockerfile`** — multi-stage Node 20 Alpine build using Next standalone output (`output: 'standalone'` added to `next.config.js`), runs as a non-root user on port 3000. Validated end-to-end: the built image serves the app (HTTP 200), calculates real routes through `/api/routing/directions`, and reverse-geocodes through `/api/geocoding/reverse`.
- **`terraform/`** — mirrors your territory-planner pattern, service name **routing-playground**: API enablement, Artifact Registry repo, server API key in Secret Manager (version-pinned, so rotating the key rolls a new revision), dedicated runtime service account, Cloud Run v2 service (1 CPU / 512Mi, scale 0–2, public), service URL as output. `terraform init/validate/fmt` all pass. `terraform/README.md` documents the three-step flow.
- **`.gitignore`** (repo had none) and `.dockerignore` — tfvars, state, `.env.local`, `node_modules` all excluded.

**Key design point:** the two API keys travel differently. The server key (`NEXTBILLION_API_KEY`) is injected at runtime from Secret Manager — never in the image. The public map key (`NEXT_PUBLIC_*`) is inlined into the client bundle at build time, so it's a Docker build arg. One trap I hit and fixed in the README: your `.env.local` has an inline comment after the key, which naive shell extraction drags along — the documented command strips it.

**Also fixed:** `npm run build` had never been run and failed type-checking (three causes: `selectors` blocks in the Rematch models that `createModel` doesn't accept — dead code since `@rematch/select` isn't installed; `@rematch/core`'s redux-4-era type augmentations, now patched via `patch-package` with a `postinstall` hook the Dockerfile honors; and two small map-component type errors). `tsc --noEmit` is clean and I re-verified the running app in the browser afterwards.

**To deploy:**
```bash
cd terraform
cp terraform.tfvars.example terraform.tfvars   # fill in the API key
terraform init
terraform apply -target=google_artifact_registry_repository.app
# then build & push per README step 2, and:
terraform apply -var image="$TAG"
```

The `routing-playground:test` image is still in your local Docker if you want to poke at it.

### CLAUDE (2026-08-20T19:01:36.516Z)

Done and live. All directions API requests now always send `option=flexible`, and the change is deployed to Cloud Run.

Two things worth knowing:

1. **`cross_border=true` had to come along.** The flexible API hard-rejects routes that cross a country border (`CrossBorderNotAllowed`) unless that parameter is set — the fast API allowed them implicitly. I caught this when an Amsterdam→Düsseldorf test failed, so both parameters are now set on every request in `src/services/routing/directionsApi.ts` (the old `needsFlexibleApi()` conditional is removed).

2. **Slightly stricter snapping**: flexible also refuses coordinates it can't snap to a road (`NoSegment`) — e.g. a click in open sea — where behavior may have differed before. The error surfaces cleanly in the Route Summary panel.

Verified locally in the browser (request URL shows `option=flexible&cross_border=true`, NL→DE route renders, 198 km / 2h 24min) and against the live service, which now returns `status: Ok` for a cross-border flexible request at https://routing-playground-7j5cx7inrq-uc.a.run.app — deployed as image tag `48e6988-flexible`. The response format is unchanged (same legs/geometry shape), so no parsing changes were needed.

 "new_string": "/**\n * Multi-select dropdown for road-feature lists (avoid / exclude)\n */\ninterface MultiSelectFeaturesProps<T extends string> {\n  value: T[];\n  optionsList: { value: T; label: string }[];\n  onChange: (event: SelectChangeEvent<T[]>) => void;\n}\n\nfunction MultiSelectFeatures<T extends string>({\n  value,\n  optionsList,\n  onChange,\n}: MultiSelectFeaturesProps<T>) {\n  const labelFor = (v: T) =>\n    optionsList.find((o) => o.value === v)?.label ?? v;\n\n  return (\n    <FormControl size=\"small\" fullWidth sx={{ mt: 0.5 }}>\n      <Select<T[]>\n        multiple\n        displayEmpty\n        value={value}\n        onChange={onChange}\n        input={<OutlinedInput />}\n        renderValue={(selected) =>\n          selected.length === 0 ? (\n            <Typography variant=\"body2\" color=\"text.disabled\">\n              None\n            </Typography>\n          ) : (\n            <Box sx={{ display: 'flex', flexWrap: 'wrap', gap: 0.5 }}>\n              {selected.map((v) => (\n                <Chip key={v} label={labelFor(v)} size=\"small\" />\n              ))}\n            </Box>\n          )\n        }\n        MenuProps={{ PaperProps: { style: { maxHeight: 320 } } }}\n      >\n        {optionsList.map(({ value: v, label }) => (\n          <MenuItem key={v} value={v} dense>\n            <Checkbox checked={value.includes(v)} size=\"small\" />\n            <ListItemText\n              primary={<Typography variant=\"body2\">{label}</Typography>}\n            />\n          </MenuItem>\n        ))}\n      </Select>\n    </FormControl>\n  );\n}\n\nexport default RoutingOptionsPanel;"
}

### CLAUDE (2026-08-20T19:53:16.907Z)

Build running in the background — I'll `terraform apply` when it pushes. Summary of what was implemented while that runs:

**Excludes + expanded avoids** (per the official NextBillion Directions API schema, which I pulled to get the authoritative enums):

- **New `exclude` support** — the strict filter: the API refuses to return a route through excluded features (vs. `avoid`, which is a soft preference that falls back if unavoidable). The UI captions explain the distinction. Options: toll roads, ferries, highways, sharp turns, U-turns, left turns, right turns, service roads. Plumbed through the types (`ExcludeOption`), the store (`exclude: []` state + `setExclude` reducer), and the API client (`exclude=a|b|c`).
- **Expanded `avoid` list** — same eight features plus tunnels (avoid-only per the docs). Dropped the old "Unpaved roads" option, which isn't a valid value for the flexible API. I left out `bbox` and `geofence_id`, which need extra inputs (bounding-box coordinates / geofence IDs) beyond a simple toggle.
- **Multiselect UI** — both lists are now compact MUI multiselect dropdowns with checkbox menu items and chips for the selected values, replacing the checkbox column.
- **Bug fixed along the way**: avoids were being joined with commas, but the API spec requires pipe separation — both parameters now use `|`.

Verified in the browser: selecting Toll roads + Ferries under Exclude sent `exclude=toll%7Cferry`, and the route re-planned from 204 km / 2h 33min to a 270 km / 3h 50min toll- and ferry-free alternative.

{
 "file_path": "/Users/[USER]/workspace/tomtom_playground/src/utils/shields.ts",
 "content": "/**\n * Road-number shields, drawn programmatically (no image assets).\n * Ported from the LONDON_COUNCILS demo and extended with US classifications\n * (Interstate / US route / state route) for NYC-area routing.\n */\nexport type ShieldKind =\n  | 'interstate'\n  | 'us-route'\n  | 'state'\n  | 'motorway'\n  | 'a-road'\n  | 'b-road'\n  | 'other';\n\nexport interface ShieldSpec {\n  label: string;\n  kind: ShieldKind;\n  /** Fill / text / border colours as [r, g, b]. */\n  fill: [number, number, number];\n  text: [number, number, number];\n  border: [number, number, number];\n}\n\nconst PALETTE: Record<ShieldKind, Pick<ShieldSpec, 'fill' | 'text' | 'border'>> = {\n  // Interstate: white on blue with red border (echoes the US shield)\n  interstate: { fill: [0, 63, 135], text: [255, 255, 255], border: [175, 30, 45] },\n  // US route: black on white\n  'us-route': { fill: [255, 255, 255], text: [17, 24, 39], border: [17, 24, 39] },\n  // State route: black on white, gray border\n  state: { fill: [255, 255, 255], text: [17, 24, 39], border: [107, 114, 128] },\n  // UK motorway: white on blue\n  motorway: { fill: [13, 63, 143], text: [255, 255, 255], border: [255, 255, 255] },\n  // UK A-road (primary route signage): yellow on green\n  'a-road': { fill: [10, 95, 56], text: [255, 212, 0], border: [255, 255, 255] },\n  // UK B-road / non-primary: black on white\n  'b-road': { fill: [255, 255, 255], text: [17, 24, 39], border: [55, 65, 81] },\n  other: { fill: [229, 231, 235], text: [31, 41, 55], border: [156, 163, 175] },\n};\n\nexport function classifyRoadRef(ref: string): ShieldKind {\n  const r = ref.trim().toUpperCase();\n  if (/^I[-\\s]?\\d+/.test(r)) return 'interstate';\n  if (/^US[-\\s]?\\d+/.test(r)) return 'us-route';\n  if (/^M\\d+/.test(r) || /^A\\d+\\(M\\)/.test(r)) return 'motorway';\n  if (/^A\\d+/.test(r)) return 'a-road';\n  if (/^B\\d+/.test(r)) return 'b-road';\n  if (/^[A-Z]{2}[-\\s]?\\d+/.test(r)) return 'state';\n  return 'other';\n}\n\nexport function shieldSpec(ref: string): ShieldSpec {\n  const label = ref.trim().toUpperCase().replace(/\\s+/g, ' ');\n  const kind = classifyRoadRef(label);\n  return { label, kind, ...PALETTE[kind] };\n}\n\n/**\n * Split a reference string into individual road numbers. NB may return\n * \"A1\", \"A1/A41\", \"I 278; NY 27\" or \"M25 (M1)\" style values.\n */\nexport function splitRoadRefs(ref?: string | null): string[] {\n  if (!ref) return [];\n  const out: string[] = [];\n  const re =\n    /\\b((?:I|US)[-\\s]?\\d{1,4}|(?:M|A|B)\\d{1,4}(?:\\(M\\))?|[A-Z]{2}[-\\s]?\\d{1,4})\\b/g;\n  for (const m of ref.toUpperCase().matchAll(re)) {\n    const label = m[1].replace(/\\s+/g, ' ');\n    if (!out.includes(label)) out.push(label);\n  }\n  return out;\n}\n\nexport function rgbCss([r, g, b]: [number, number, number]): string {\n  return `rgb(${r},${g},${b})`;\n}\n"
}

 "content": "/**\n * Inline-SVG road shield (US Interstate/US/state and UK M/A/B classification).\n * Ported from the LONDON_COUNCILS demo.\n */\n'use client';\n\nimport React from 'react';\nimport { rgbCss, shieldSpec } from '@/utils/shields';\n\ninterface ShieldProps {\n  refNo: string;\n  height?: number;\n}\n\nexport const Shield: React.FC<ShieldProps> = ({ refNo, height = 16 }) => {\n  const s = shieldSpec(refNo);\n  const fontSize = height * 0.68;\n  const width = Math.max(\n    height * 1.4,\n    s.label.length * fontSize * 0.62 + height * 0.5\n  );\n  return (\n    <svg\n      width={width}\n      height={height}\n      viewBox={`0 0 ${width} ${height}`}\n      role=\"img\"\n      aria-label={`Road ${s.label}`}\n      style={{ display: 'inline-block', verticalAlign: 'middle', flexShrink: 0 }}\n    >\n      <rect\n        x={0.75}\n        y={0.75}\n        width={width - 1.5}\n        height={height - 1.5}\n        rx={height * 0.2}\n        fill={rgbCss(s.fill)}\n        stroke={rgbCss(s.border)}\n        strokeWidth={1.5}\n      />\n      <text\n        x={width / 2}\n        y={height / 2}\n        dominantBaseline=\"central\"\n        textAnchor=\"middle\"\n        fontFamily=\"Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif\"\n        fontWeight={700}\n        fontSize={fontSize}\n        fill={rgbCss(s.text)}\n      >\n        {s.label}\n      </text>\n    </svg>\n  );\n};\n\nexport default Shield;\n"
}

{
 "file_path": "/Users/[USER]/workspace/tomtom_playground/src/app/api/routing/navigation/route.ts",
 "content": "/**\n * API Route: Proxy to NextBillion.ai Navigation API\n * Returns turn-by-turn maneuver instructions for an existing route geometry.\n * The route shape is passed via `original_shape` (POST — encoded polylines\n * are far too long for a GET query string).\n */\nimport { NextRequest, NextResponse } from 'next/server';\n\nconst NB_API_KEY = process.env.NEXTBILLION_API_KEY || '';\nconst NB_NAV_URL = 'https://api.nextbillion.io/navigation/json';\n\ninterface NavigationRequestBody {\n  /** Encoded polyline of the route. */\n  polyline: string;\n  precision?: 5 | 6;\n  lang?: string;\n}\n\nexport async function POST(request: NextRequest) {\n  if (!NB_API_KEY) {\n    return NextResponse.json(\n      { status: 'Error', msg: 'API key not configured' },\n      { status: 500 }\n    );\n  }\n\n  let body: NavigationRequestBody;\n  try {\n    body = await request.json();\n  } catch {\n    return NextResponse.json(\n      { status: 'Error', msg: 'Invalid JSON body' },\n      { status: 400 }\n    );\n  }\n\n  if (typeof body.polyline !== 'string' || body.polyline.length < 4) {\n    return NextResponse.json(\n      { status: 'Error', msg: 'polyline required' },\n      { status: 400 }\n    );\n  }\n\n  const shapeType = body.precision === 6 ? 'polyline6' : 'polyline';\n  const lang =\n    typeof body.lang === 'string' && /^[a-zA-Z-]{2,10}$/.test(body.lang)\n      ? body.lang\n      : 'en-US';\n\n  try {\n    const response = await fetch(`${NB_NAV_URL}?key=${encodeURIComponent(NB_API_KEY)}`, {\n      method: 'POST',\n      headers: {\n        'Content-Type': 'application/json',\n        'Accept': 'application/json',\n      },\n      body: JSON.stringify({\n        original_shape: body.polyline,\n        original_shape_type: shapeType,\n        geometry: 'polyline',\n        lang,\n      }),\n    });\n\n    const data = await response.json();\n\n    return NextResponse.json(data, {\n      status: response.status,\n      headers: {\n        'Cache-Control': 'no-store, max-age=0',\n      },\n    });\n  } catch (error) {\n    console.error('Navigation API error:', error);\n    return NextResponse.json(\n      { status: 'Error', msg: 'Failed to fetch navigation instructions' },\n      { status: 500 }\n    );\n  }\n}\n"
}

 "content": "/**\n * NextBillion.ai Navigation API Client\n * Fetches turn-by-turn maneuver instructions for an existing route geometry.\n */\n\nconst API_ENDPOINT = '/api/routing/navigation';\n\nexport interface NavStep {\n  index: number;\n  instruction: string;\n  maneuverType: string;\n  modifier?: string;\n  distanceM: number;\n  durationSec: number;\n  name?: string;\n  reference?: string;\n  /** [lng, lat] of the maneuver point. */\n  location: [number, number];\n}\n\nexport interface NavigationResult {\n  distanceM: number;\n  durationSec: number;\n  steps: NavStep[];\n}\n\n/**\n * Requests turn-by-turn instructions for an encoded route polyline.\n * Throws with a readable message on failure.\n */\nexport async function fetchNavigation(\n  polyline: string,\n  precision: 5 | 6 = 5\n): Promise<NavigationResult> {\n  const response = await fetch(API_ENDPOINT, {\n    method: 'POST',\n    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },\n    body: JSON.stringify({ polyline, precision }),\n  });\n\n  let data: any;\n  try {\n    data = await response.json();\n  } catch {\n    throw new Error(`Navigation request failed (${response.status})`);\n  }\n\n  const statusOk = !data?.status || String(data.status).toLowerCase() === 'ok';\n  const route = data?.routes?.[0];\n  if (!response.ok || !statusOk || !route) {\n    throw new Error(\n      data?.msg ?? data?.message ?? `Navigation request failed (${response.status})`\n    );\n  }\n\n  const steps: NavStep[] = [];\n  let idx = 0;\n  for (const leg of route.legs ?? []) {\n    for (const st of leg.steps ?? []) {\n      const m = st?.maneuver ?? {};\n      const c = m.coordinate ?? st?.start_location ?? {};\n      steps.push({\n        index: idx++,\n        instruction: String(m.instruction ?? ''),\n        maneuverType: String(m.maneuver_type ?? m.type ?? ''),\n        modifier: m.modifier ? String(m.modifier) : undefined,\n        distanceM: Number(st?.distance?.value ?? st?.distance ?? 0),\n        durationSec: Number(st?.duration?.value ?? st?.duration ?? 0),\n        name: st?.name || undefined,\n        reference: st?.reference || undefined,\n        location: [Number(c.longitude), Number(c.latitude)],\n      });\n    }\n  }\n\n  return {\n    distanceM: Number(route.distance ?? 0),\n    durationSec: Number(route.duration ?? 0),\n    steps,\n  };\n}\n"
}
```

'').toLowerCase();\n  if (t === 'depart') return '●';\n  if (t === 'arrive') return '⚑';\n  if (t.includes('roundabout') || t.includes('rotary')) return '↻';\n  if (t === 'merge') return '⤵';\n  if (t === 'fork' || t.includes('ramp') || t === 'on ramp' || t === 'off ramp') return '⑂';\n  if (t === 'uturn' || mod.includes('uturn')) return '⤶';\n  if (mod.includes('sharp left')) return '↰';\n  if (mod.includes('sharp right')) return '↱';\n  if (mod.includes('slight left')) return '↖';\n  if (mod.includes('slight right')) return '↗';\n  if (mod.includes('left')) return '←';\n  if (mod.includes('right')) return '→';\n  if (t === 'continue' || t === 'new name' || mod.includes('straight')) return '↑';\n  return '•';\n}\n\ninterface SummaryItem {\n  label: string;\n  isRef: boolean;\n}\n\n/**\n * Ordered \"main roads\" summary: one entry per step, using the step's road\n * reference when it has one and the road name otherwise, with consecutive\n * duplicates collapsed.\n */\nfunction routeSummary(steps: NavStep[]): SummaryItem[] {\n  const out: SummaryItem[] = [];\n  for (const st of steps) {\n    const refs = splitRoadRefs(st.reference);\n    const name = st.name?.trim();\n    const item: SummaryItem | null = refs.length\n      ? routeSummary(nav.steps) : [];\n\n  return (\n    <Paper variant=\"outlined\" sx={{ borderRadius: 2, overflow: 'hidden' }}>\n      {/* Header */}\n      <Box\n        sx={{\n          px: 2,\n          py: 1.5,\n          display: 'flex',\n          alignItems: 'center',\n          justifyContent: 'space-between',\n          gap: 1,\n        }}\n      >\n        <Box>\n          <Typography variant=\"subtitle1\" fontWeight={600}>\n            Directions\n          </Typography>\n          {nav && status === 'done' && (\n            <Typography variant=\"caption\" color=\"text.secondary\">\n              {formatDistance(nav.distanceM)} · {formatDuration(nav.durationSec)} ·{' '}\n              {nav.steps.length} steps\n            </Typography>\n          )}\n        </Box>\n        {status === 'idle' || status === 'error' ? (\n          <Button\n            variant=\"contained\"\n            size=\"small\"\n            startIcon={<DirectionsIcon />}\n            onClick={handleGetDirections}\n            disabled={!encodedPolyline}\n          >\n            Get Directions\n          </Button>\n        ) : status === 'done' ? (\n          <IconButton\n            size=\"small\"\n            aria-label=\"Clear directions\"\n            onClick={() => {\n              setStatus('idle');\n              setNav(null);\n              setActiveStep(null);\n            }}\n          >\n            <CloseIcon fontSize=\"small\" />\n          </IconButton>\n        ) : null}\n      </Box>\n\n      {/* Loading */}\n      {status === 'loading' && (\n        <Box sx={{ px: 2, pb: 2, display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 1 }}>\n          <CircularProgress size={16} />\n          <Typography variant=\"body2\" color=\"primary\">\n            Fetching maneuvers from NextBillion.ai…\n          </Typography>\n        </Box>\n      )}\n\n      {/* Error */}\n      {status === 'error' && error && (\n        <Typography variant=\"body2\" color=\"error\" sx={{ px: 2, pb: 2 }}>\n          {error}\n        </Typography>\n      )}\n\n      {/* Main-roads summary */}\n      {status === 'done' && nav && summary.length > 0 && (\n        <>\n          <Divider />\n          <Box sx={{ px: 2, py: 1.5, bgcolor: 'grey.50' }}>\n            <Typography\n              variant=\"caption\"\n              fontWeight={600}\n              color=\"text.secondary\"\n              display=\"block\"\n              gutterBottom\n            >\n              Route summary (main roads)\n            </Typography>\n            <Box\n              sx={{\n                display: 'flex',\n                flexWrap: 'wrap',\n                alignItems: 'center',\n                columnGap: 0.75,\n                rowGap: 0.5,\n              }}\n            >\n              {summary.map((it, i) => (\n                <Box\n                  key={`${it.label}-${i}`}\n                  component=\"span\"\n                  sx={{ display: 'inline-flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 0.75 }}\n                >\n                  {i > 0 && (\n                    <Typography Ported from the LONDON_COUNCILS demo.\n *\n * Road-shield density: the TomTom style shows shields for minor roads from\n * low zooms, which is far too dense at a city-wide view. Raise the minimum\n * zoom per road class, repeat shields less often along a road, and render\n * the remaining shields a little larger.\n */\nimport type {\n  StyleSpecification,\n  SymbolLayerSpecification,\n} from 'maplibre-gl';\n\nconst SHIELD_MINZOOM: Record<string, number> = {\n  Motorway: 7,\n  'International road': 8,\n  'Major road': 10,\n  'Secondary road': 11,\n  'Connecting road': 12,\n  'Major local road': 13,\n  'Local road': 14,\n  'Minor local road': 15,\n};\nconst SHIELD_SPACING_PX = 600;\nconst SHIELD_PADDING_PX = 20;\n// Render shields 25% larger than the style default (icon + text scale together).\nconst SHIELD_SCALE = 1.25;\n\nfunction scaleLayoutValue(v: unknown, fallback: number): unknown {\n  if (typeof v === 'number') return v * SHIELD_SCALE;\n  if (Array.isArray(v)) return ['*', v, SHIELD_SCALE];\n  return fallback * SHIELD_SCALE;\n}\n\n// The v2 (street-light / traffic) style has a single \"roads\" source-layer with\n// a `category` attribute and a zoom-stepped filter; these are the zooms at\n// which each category's shields become visible.\nconst V2_SHIELD_STEPS: Array<[number, string[]]> = [\n  [0, ['motorway', 'trunk']],\n  [10, ['motorway', 'trunk', 'primary']],\n  [12, ['motorway', 'trunk', 'primary', 'secondary']],\n];\nconst V2_ALL_ROADS_FROM_ZOOM = 14;\n\nexport function thinShields(style: StyleSpecification): StyleSpecification {\n  return {\n    ...style,\n    layers: style.layers.map((l) => {\n      if (l.type !== 'symbol') return l;\n      const src =\n        'source-layer' in l && typeof l['source-layer'] === 'string'\n          ? l['source-layer']\n          : '';\n      const layout = (l.layout ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>;\n      const denser = {\n        ...layout,\n        'symbol-spacing': SHIELD_SPACING_PX,\n        'icon-padding': SHIELD_PADDING_PX,\n        'icon-size': scaleLayoutValue(layout['icon-size'], 1),\n        ...('text-field' in layout\n          ? { 'text-size': scaleLayoutValue(layout['text-size'], 16) }\n          : {}),\n      } as SymbolLayerSpecification['layout'];\n      // v1 style (basic_main): one layer per road class, \"Shield<Class><n>\".\n      if (l.id.startsWith('Shield')) {\n        const cls = src.replace(/^Toll /, '').replace(/ tunnel$/, '');\n        const mz = SHIELD_MINZOOM[cls];\n        return {\n          ...l,\n          ...(mz != null ? { minzoom: Math.max(l.minzoom ?? 0, mz) } : {}),\n          layout: denser,\n        };\n      }\n      // v2 style: \"TransitLabels - Road Shield n\" on the \"roads\" source-layer.\n      if (/Road Shield/i.test(l.id) && src === 'roads') {\n        const f = l.filter as unknown[] | undefined;\n        const hasClause = Array.isArray(f) && f[0] === 'all' ? f[1] : undefined;\n        const step: unknown[] = ['step', ['zoom']];\n        V2_SHIELD_STEPS.forEach(([z, cats], i) => {\n          if (i > 0) step.push(z);\n          step.push(['match', ['get', 'category'], cats, true, false]);\n        });\n        step.push(V2_ALL_ROADS_FROM_ZOOM, [\n          'match',\n          ['get', 'category'],\n          ['street'],\n          false,\n          true,\n        ]);\n        const filter = hasClause ? ['all', hasClause, step] : ['all', step];\n        return { ...l, filter: filter as typeof l.filter, layout: denser };\n      }\n      return l;\n    }),\n  };\n}\n"

### CLAUDE (2026-08-20T20:09:50.147Z)

While that builds, everything requested is implemented and verified locally:

1. **NYC start view** — the map now opens centered on New York City at zoom 11 (`ui` model initial viewport).

2. **Turn-by-turn directions panel** (ported from the LONDON_COUNCILS demo):
   - A **Directions** panel appears in the sidebar once a route exists, with a "Get Directions" button that POSTs the route's encoded polyline to a new `/api/routing/navigation` proxy (NextBillion Navigation API via `original_shape`, key stays server-side).
   - The panel shows totals (29 km · 1h 50min · 35 steps for my Manhattan→JFK test), the demo's **"Route summary (main roads)"** strip (NY-9A / 12th Ave / … with shields), and the full maneuver list — colored glyph icons per maneuver type, instruction text, distance/duration/road name per step.
   - **Highway shields** render inline as SVGs; I extended the demo's UK-only classification (M/A/B) with US classes — Interstate (blue/red), US routes, and state routes (NY 27, NY 878, I-678 all render correctly).
   - Clicking a step zooms the map to that maneuver point (verified — West St in Chelsea at zoom 15).
   - Instructions clear automatically when the route changes.
   - Fixed a flexbox bug found during testing: the panel's `overflow: hidden` let the sidebar's flex column crush it to zero height on short windows (`flexShrink: 0`).

3. **Basemap shield density** — ported the demo's `thinShields` style transform: the style JSON is fetched and rewritten before rendering, raising per-road-class minimum zooms, spacing shields 600px apart, and scaling the survivors 25% larger. It handles both the `basic_main` style and the v2 traffic style layer naming.

I'll finish the Cloud Run deploy when the image push completes.

 "content": "/**\n * Maneuver Markers - dots at each turn-by-turn maneuver point, with an\n * info window showing the instruction on hover/click.\n * Rendered only while navigation instructions are loaded.\n */\n'use client';\n\nimport React, { useMemo, useState } from 'react';\nimport { Marker, Popup } from 'react-map-gl';\nimport { Box, Typography } from '@mui/material';\nimport { useAppSelector } from '@/store/hooks';\nimport { formatDistance, formatDuration } from '@/utils/formatting';\nimport type { NavStep } from '@/types/routing';\n\nexport const ManeuverMarkers: React.FC = () => {\n  const navigation = useAppSelector((state) => state.route.navigation);\n  const [openStep, setOpenStep] = useState<NavStep | null>(null);\n  const [pinned, setPinned] = useState(false);\n\n  const steps = useMemo(\n    () =>\n      (navigation?.steps ?? []).filter(\n        (st) => Number.isFinite(st.location[0]) && Number.isFinite(st.location[1])\n      ),\n    [navigation]\n  );\n\n  if (steps.length === 0) {\n    return null;\n  }\n\n  const showPopup = (st: NavStep, pin: boolean) => {\n    setOpenStep(st);\n    setPinned(pin);\n  };\n\n  const hidePopup = (onlyUnpinned: boolean) => {\n    if (onlyUnpinned && pinned) return;\n    setOpenStep(null);\n    setPinned(false);\n  };\n\n  return (\n    <>\n      {steps.map((st) => (\n        <Marker\n          key={st.index}\n          longitude={st.location[0]}\n          latitude={st.location[1]}\n          anchor=\"center\"\n        >\n          <Box\n            onMouseEnter={() => {\n              if (!pinned) showPopup(st, false);\n            }}\n            onMouseLeave={() => hidePopup(true)}\n            onClick={(e) => {\n              e.stopPropagation();\n              if (pinned && openStep?.index === st.index) {\n                hidePopup(false);\n              } else {\n                showPopup(st, true);\n              }\n            }}\n            sx={{\n              width: 12,\n              height: 12,\n              borderRadius: '50%',\n              bgcolor: 'success.main',\n              border: '2px solid white',\n              boxShadow: '0 1px 3px rgba(0,0,0,0.4)',\n              cursor: 'pointer',\n              '&:hover': {\n                bgcolor: 'success.dark',\n              },\n            }}\n          />\n        </Marker>\n      ))}\n\n      {openStep && (\n        <Popup\n          longitude={openStep.location[0]}\n          latitude={openStep.location[1]}\n          anchor=\"bottom\"\n          offset={10}\n          closeButton={pinned}\n          closeOnClick={false}\n          onClose={() => hidePopup(false)}\n          maxWidth=\"280px\"\n        >\n          <Box sx={{ pr: pinned ? 1.5 : 0 }}>\n            <Typography variant=\"body2\" fontWeight={600}>\n              {openStep.index + 1}. {openStep.instruction || openStep.maneuverType}\n            </Typography>\n            <Typography variant=\"caption\" color=\"text.secondary\">\n              {openStep.distanceM > 0\n                ? `${formatDistance(openStep.distanceM)} · ${formatDuration(openStep.durationSec)}`\n                : 'arrive'}\n              {openStep.name ? ` · ${openStep.name}` : ''}\n              {openStep.reference ? ` (${openStep.reference})` : ''}\n            </Typography>\n          </Box>\n        </Popup>\n      )}\n    </>\n  );\n};\n\nexport default ManeuverMarkers;\n"
}

### CLAUDE (2026-08-20T22:59:06.283Z)

Feature done and verified locally; the deploy finishes when the build lands. What was added:

- **Maneuver markers**: when directions are fetched, every maneuver point gets a small green dot marker along the route (`src/components/map/ManeuverMarkers.tsx`). Hovering a dot opens an info window with the step number, instruction, distance/duration, and road name; clicking pins the popup open (with a close button) so it survives mouse-out. Markers disappear when directions are cleared or the route changes.
- **Shared navigation state**: the navigation result moved from `DirectionsPanel`'s local state into the route store (`route.navigation`, with the `NavStep` types now in `types/routing.ts`), so the sidebar panel and map markers render from the same source. `setResult`/`clearRoute` clear it automatically, which is what removes the markers on route changes.

I'll confirm the Cloud Run rollout when the image push completes.

Accepts the same query\n * parameters as the directions proxy (origin, destination, waypoints,\n * mode, avoid, ...) and forwards them with the server-side API key.\n */\nimport { NextRequest, NextResponse } from 'next/server';\n\nconst NB_API_KEY = process.env.NEXTBILLION_API_KEY || '';\nconst NB_NAV_URL = 'https://api.nextbillion.io/navigation/json';\n\nexport async function GET(request: NextRequest) {\n  if (!NB_API_KEY) {\n    return NextResponse.json(\n      { status: 'Error', msg: 'API key not configured' },\n      { status: 500 }\n    );\n  }\n\n  const params = new URLSearchParams(request.nextUrl.searchParams);\n  params.set('key', NB_API_KEY);\n\n  try {\n    const response = await fetch(`${NB_NAV_URL}?${params}`, {\n      headers: {\n        'Accept': 'application/json',\n      },\n    });\n\n    const data = await response.json();\n\n    return NextResponse.json(data, {\n      status: response.status,\n      headers: {\n        'Cache-Control': 'no-store, max-age=0',\n      },\n    });\n  } catch (error) {\n    console.error('Navigation API error:', error);\n    return NextResponse.json(\n      { status: 'Error', msg: 'Failed to fetch navigation instructions' },\n      { status: 500 }\n    );\n  }\n}\n"
}
```

 "content": "/**\n * NextBillion.ai Navigation API Client\n * Fetches turn-by-turn maneuver instructions using the same request\n * parameters as the Directions API (origin, destination, waypoints, options).\n */\nimport type { DirectionsRequest, NavStep, NavigationResult } from '@/types/routing';\nimport { directionsApi } from './directionsApi';\n\nconst API_ENDPOINT = '/api/routing/navigation';\n\nexport type { NavStep, NavigationResult };\n\n/**\n * Requests turn-by-turn instructions for a route request.\n * Throws with a readable message on failure.\n */\nexport async function fetchNavigation(\n  request: DirectionsRequest\n): Promise<NavigationResult> {\n  const params = directionsApi.buildParams(request);\n  const response = await fetch(`${API_ENDPOINT}?${params}`);\n\n  let data: any;\n  try {\n    data = await response.json();\n  } catch {\n    throw new Error(`Navigation request failed (${response.status})`);\n  }\n\n  const statusOk = !data?.status || String(data.status).toLowerCase() === 'ok';\n  const route = data?.routes?.[0];\n  if (!response.ok || !statusOk || !route) {\n    throw new Error(\n      data?.msg ?? data?.message ?? `Navigation request failed (${response.status})`\n    );\n  }\n\n  const steps: NavStep[] = [];\n  let idx = 0;\n  for (const leg of route.legs ?? []) {\n    for (const st of leg.steps ?? []) {\n      const m = st?.maneuver ?? {};\n      const c = m.coordinate ?? st?.start_location ?? {};\n      steps.push({\n        index: idx++,\n        instruction: String(m.instruction ?? ''),\n        maneuverType: String(m.maneuver_type ?? m.type ?? ''),\n        modifier: m.modifier ? String(m.modifier) : undefined,\n        distanceM: Number(st?.distance?.value ?? st?.distance ?? 0),\n        durationSec: Number(st?.duration?.value ?? st?.duration ?? 0),\n        name: st?.name || undefined,\n        reference: st?.reference || undefined,\n        location: [Number(c.longitude), Number(c.latitude)],\n      });\n    }\n  }\n\n  return {\n    distanceM: Number(route.distance ?? 0),\n    durationSec: Number(route.duration ?? 0),\n    steps,\n  };\n}\n"
}

### CLAUDE (2026-08-20T23:02:24.719Z)

Build running. The change summary:

- **Navigation proxy** (`/api/routing/navigation`) is now a GET pass-through — same shape as the directions proxy — forwarding the query string to `navigation/json` with the server key. The polyline/`original_shape` flow is gone.
- **Shared parameter builder**: `directionsApi.buildParams()` is now public and the navigation client uses it directly, so a navigation request carries *exactly* what the directions request carries — origin, destination, waypoints, mode, avoid, exclude, `option=flexible`, `cross_border=true`, route type, truck parameters.
- **DirectionsPanel** builds the request from store state (waypoints + routing options) instead of pulling the encoded geometry from the previous directions response.

Two nice side effects, verified against the live NB API: the avoid/exclude selections now genuinely shape the turn-by-turn output (23 vs 30 vs 18 steps in my three test combos), and the Times Square→JFK case that the Navigation API previously refused to shape-match via polyline now works. I'll finish the Cloud Run rollout when the push completes.

### CLAUDE (2026-08-20T23:03:51.339Z)

Deployed and verified live — the navigation endpoint on https://routing-playground-7j5cx7inrq-uc.a.run.app now accepts the same parameters as the directions API (the live test returned 23 steps for Times Square→JFK with `option=flexible&cross_border=true`), and this revision also carries the maneuver markers with their info windows from the previous change.

Recap of what's now live:
- **Navigation = directions parameters**: the panel's "Get Directions" sends origin/destination/waypoints plus all routing options (mode, avoid, exclude, route type, truck params, `option=flexible`, `cross_border=true`) through a shared parameter builder — no more polyline hand-off, and avoid/exclude selections now shape the turn-by-turn results.
- **Maneuver markers**: green dots at every maneuver point while directions are shown, with hover info windows (instruction, distance, duration, road) and click-to-pin; they clear when the route changes or directions are dismissed.

### CLAUDE (2026-08-20T23:09:38.983Z)

Deployed and verified live at https://routing-playground-7j5cx7inrq-uc.a.run.app (revision `48e6988-departure`) — the live navigation endpoint accepts `departure_time` (16 steps returned for a +2h departure test) and the root serves fine.

This revision carries all three changes:

1. **Departure date/time control** — a datetime picker in Routing Options ("Departure — blank departs now"). Setting it stores the time in routing options, which automatically flows into `departure_time` (epoch seconds) on **both** directions and navigation requests via the shared parameter builder — and changing it triggers a route recalculation. Clearing the field departs now.

2. **Floating maneuver panel** — the turn-by-turn list moved out of the left sidebar into its own panel docked top-right over the map (mirroring the LONDON_COUNCILS placement), with the totals header, main-roads shield summary, scrollable step list, step-click zoom, and a close button that also clears the map markers. The sidebar keeps only a compact "Get Directions"/"Refresh" control.

3. **Shields above the route** — ported the demo's label-anchoring approach: `firstLabelLayerId()` finds the style's first text-label layer and the route polyline layers are inserted `beforeId` it, so highway shields and street names render above the route line in both map styles.

{
 "file_path": "/Users/[USER]/workspace/tomtom_playground/src/utils/spriteShields.ts",
 "content": "/**\n * Road shields drawn from the basemap's own sprite sheet, so the shields in\n * the maneuver list match the glyphs rendered on the map exactly.\n *\n * The map style picks sprite icons from tile data (shield_icon_* feature\n * properties); the list only has the road ref text, so this module maps a\n * classified ref (I/US/state, UK M/A/B) onto the equivalent sprite icons.\n */\nimport { classifyRoadRef } from './shields';\n\nexport interface SpriteIconMeta {\n  x: number;\n  y: number;\n  width: number;\n  height: number;\n  pixelRatio: number;\n}\n\nexport interface SpriteSheet {\n  url: string;\n  meta: Record<string, SpriteIconMeta>;\n  /** Sheet dimensions in device pixels (computed from icon extents). */\n  sheetW: number;\n  sheetH: number;\n}\n\n// Keep in sync with the style URLs in MapContainer\nconst SPRITE_BASE = 'https://api.nextbillion.io/tt/style/1/sprite/25.2.3-0/sprite@2x';\n\nlet cached: Promise<SpriteSheet> | null = null;\n\nexport function loadSpriteSheet(): Promise<SpriteSheet> {\n  if (!cached) {\n    const key = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_NEXTBILLION_API_KEY ?? '';\n    const qs = `?key=${encodeURIComponent(key)}&map=basic_main`;\n    cached = fetch(`${SPRITE_BASE}.json${qs}`)\n      .then((r) => {\n        if (!r.ok) throw new Error(`sprite fetch failed (${r.status})`);\n        return r.json();\n      })\n      .then((meta: Record<string, SpriteIconMeta>) => {\n        let sheetW = 0;\n        let sheetH = 0;\n        for (const m of Object.values(meta)) {\n          sheetW = Math.max(sheetW, m.x + m.width);\n          sheetH = Math.max(sheetH, m.y + m.height);\n        }\n        return { url: `${SPRITE_BASE}.png${qs}`, meta, sheetW, sheetH };\n      });\n    // Allow a retry on failure instead of caching the rejection\n    cached.catch(() => {\n      cached = null;\n    });\n  }\n  return cached;\n}\n\nexport interface ShieldGlyph {\n  name: string;\n  icon: SpriteIconMeta;\n  text: string;\n  textColor: string;\n  /** Vertical text offset as a fraction of icon height (interstate crest). */\n  textOffsetY: number;\n}\n\n/**\n * Finds the best width variant for a sprite base name: icons come in\n * \"<base>-<n>\" variants sized for n characters. Prefers the smallest\n * variant that fits the text, else the widest available.\n */\nfunction pickVariant(\n  meta: Record<string, SpriteIconMeta>,\n  base: string,\n  textLen: number\n): string | null {\n  const variants: Array<{ n: number; name: string }> = [];\n  for (const name of Object.keys(meta)) {\n    if (name.startsWith(`${base}-`)) {\n      const n = Number(name.slice(base.length + 1));\n      if (Number.isFinite(n)) variants.push({ n, name });\n    }\n  }\n  if (!variants.length) return null;\n  variants.sort((a, b) => a.n - b.n);\n  const fitting = variants.find((v) => v.n >= textLen);\n  return (fitting ?? variants[variants.length - 1]).name;\n}\n\nexport function pickShieldGlyph(\n  ref: string,\n  sheet: SpriteSheet\n): ShieldGlyph | null {\n  const label = ref.trim().toUpperCase().replace(/\\s+/g, ' ');\n  const kind = classifyRoadRef(label);\n  // \"I 278\" -> \"278\", \"NY 25A\" -> \"25A\"; UK refs keep the letter (\"M25\")\n  const num = label.replace(/^[A-Z]+[-\\s]?/, '') || label;\n\n  let bases: string[];\n  let text = num;\n  let textColor = '#111827';\n  let textOffsetY = 0;\n\n  switch (kind) {\n    case 'interstate':\n      bases = ['us3-blue2-white'];\n      textColor = '#fff';\n      textOffsetY = 0.08; // clear the red crest\n      break;\n    case 'us-route':\n      bases = ['usa-highway-5450', 'us1-white-black'];\n      break;\n    case 'state': {\n      const st = label.slice(0, 2).toLowerCase();\n      // Per-state markers are named usa-<st>-<id>; find any icon for the state\n      const stateBase = Object.keys(sheet.meta)\n        .filter((n) => n.startsWith(`usa-${st}-`))\n        .map((n) => n.replace(/-\\d+$/, ''))[0];\n      bases = stateBase ? [stateBase, 'us2-white-black'] : ['us2-white-black'];\n      break;\n    }\n    case 'motorway':\n      bases = ['rectangle-blue2-white'];\n      textColor = '#fff';\n      text = label;\n      break;\n    case 'a-road':\n      bases = ['rectangle-green2-white'];\n      textColor = '#fff';\n      text = label;\n      break;\n    case 'b-road':\n      bases = ['rectangle-white-black'];\n      text = label;\n      break;\n    default:\n      bases = ['rectangle-white-black'];\n      text = label;\n  }\n\n  for (const base of bases) {\n    const name = pickVariant(sheet.meta, base, text.length);\n    if (name) {\n      return { name, icon: sheet.meta[name], text, textColor, textOffsetY };\n    }\n  }\n  return null;\n}\n"
}

 "content": "/**\n * Road shield rendered from the basemap's sprite sheet, so list shields\n * match the glyphs on the map exactly. Falls back to the drawn SVG shield\n * while the sprite loads (or if no suitable icon exists).\n */\n'use client';\n\nimport React, { useEffect, useState } from 'react';\nimport { Shield } from '../sidebar/Shield';\nimport {\n  loadSpriteSheet,\n  pickShieldGlyph,\n  SpriteSheet,\n} from '@/utils/spriteShields';\n\nlet sheetState: SpriteSheet | null = null;\n\nfunction useSpriteSheet(): SpriteSheet | null {\n  const [sheet, setSheet] = useState<SpriteSheet | null>(sheetState);\n  useEffect(() => {\n    if (sheet) return;\n    let cancelled = false;\n    loadSpriteSheet()\n      .then((s) => {\n        sheetState = s;\n        if (!cancelled) setSheet(s);\n      })\n      .catch(() => {\n        // keep SVG fallback\n      });\n    return () => {\n      cancelled = true;\n    };\n  }, [sheet]);\n  return sheet;\n}\n\ninterface SpriteShieldProps {\n  refNo: string;\n  height?: number;\n}\n\nexport const SpriteShield: React.FC<SpriteShieldProps> = ({\n  refNo,\n  height = 24,\n}) => {\n  const sheet = useSpriteSheet();\n  const glyph = sheet ? pickShieldGlyph(refNo, sheet) : null;\n\n  if (!sheet || !glyph) {\n    return <Shield refNo={refNo} height={height} />;\n  }\n\n  const { icon } = glyph;\n  const pr = icon.pixelRatio || 1;\n  const scale = height / (icon.height / pr);\n  const width = (icon.width / pr) * scale;\n\n  return (\n    <span\n      role=\"img\"\n      aria-label={`Road ${refNo}`}\n      style={{\n        position: 'relative',\n        display: 'inline-block',\n        width,\n        height,\n        flexShrink: 0,\n        verticalAlign: 'middle',\n      }}\n    >\n      <span\n        style={{\n          position: 'absolute',\n          inset: 0,\n          backgroundImage: `url(\"${sheet.url}\")`,\n          backgroundRepeat: 'no-repeat',\n          backgroundPosition: `${(-icon.x / pr) * scale}px ${(-icon.y / pr) * scale}px`,\n          backgroundSize: `${(sheet.sheetW / pr) * scale}px ${(sheet.sheetH / pr) * scale}px`,\n        }}\n      />\n      <span\n        style={{\n          position: 'absolute',\n          inset: 0,\n          display: 'flex',\n          alignItems: 'center',\n          justifyContent: 'center',\n          paddingTop: glyph.textOffsetY * height,\n          fontFamily: 'Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif',\n          fontWeight: 700,\n          fontSize: Math.max(9, height * 0.42),\n          lineHeight: 1,\n          color: glyph.textColor,\n        }}\n      >\n        {glyph.text}\n      </span>\n    </span>\n  );\n};\n\nexport default SpriteShield;\n"
}
```

### CLAUDE (2026-08-20T23:18:20.150Z)

Yes — and it's implemented and verified locally. How it works:

- The map draws its shields from the style's **sprite sheet**, choosing icons via tile-data properties. The list only has the road ref text, so I added `src/utils/spriteShields.ts`, which loads the same sprite sheet (JSON + PNG, cached once) and maps a classified ref onto the equivalent sprite icon: Interstates → the `us3` red-crest/blue glyph, US routes → the US-highway outline, state routes → the actual per-state marker when the sprite has one (`usa-ny-…` etc., generic square otherwise), UK M/A/B → the blue/green/white rectangles. Each family has width variants sized per digit count, and the picker chooses the best fit.
- `SpriteShield` (`src/components/map/SpriteShield.tsx`) renders the icon as a scaled background-crop of the sprite PNG with the road number overlaid (white on Interstates, offset below the crest; black elsewhere). While the sprite loads — or if no suitable icon exists — it falls back to the previous SVG shield, so the list never shows a gap.
- The directions overlay now uses `SpriteShield` in both the main-roads summary and the step rows.

Verified side by side in the browser: the panel's I-78/I-278 shields are the identical glyph the map draws for those roads, and NY-878 matches the map's state-route square. I'll finish the Cloud Run deploy when the image push lands.

### CLAUDE (2026-08-21T12:56:41.009Z)

Feature complete and verified locally; deploy finishes when the push lands. What was implemented:

- **`road_info=toll_cost` on every request** — added in the shared parameter builder, so directions and navigation both send it.
- **Cost range**: the directions response's `road_info.toll_cost` (min/max/currency) is parsed into `RouteResult.tollCost` and shown in the Directions panel header as an amber "Tolls $7.46–$12.03" line (currency-symbol aware, collapses to a single value when min = max, hidden on toll-free routes).
- **Where tolls are active**: one discovery along the way — the Navigation API returns an *empty* `road_info` object, so the per-location signal actually comes from each step's `intersections[].classes` containing `'toll'`. Steps traversing tolled segments get `hasToll` and render an outlined amber "Toll" chip next to the instruction, marking exactly where the tolls occur in the maneuver list (verified on the Queens–Midtown Tunnel route: the I-495 entry step and the continuation carry the chip; city streets don't).

I'll confirm the Cloud Run rollout when the image push completes.

### CLAUDE (2026-08-22T00:10:00.387Z)

The Navigation API does return lane-level data, and it's rich enough for real lane-guidance UI. Each step's `intersections[]` can carry a `lanes` array, one entry per physical lane ordered left-to-right across the roadway:

```json
"lanes": [
  {"indications": ["left", "straight"], "valid": true},
  {"indications": ["straight"],          "valid": true},
  {"indications": ["straight", "right"], "valid": false}
]
```

- **`indications`** — the arrow(s) painted on that lane: `straight`, `left`, `right`, `slight left/right`, `sharp left/right`, `uturn`, `none` (unmarked). A lane can have several (e.g. straight-or-right).
- **`valid`** — whether that lane works for *this* route's maneuver.

On the Hoboken test route, 8 intersections carried lane data — e.g. "Turn left onto Willow Ave" approaches on `[left|straight ✓][straight][straight|right]`.

From that, the maneuver list could show:

1. **A lane-diagram strip per step** (the Google Maps/Waze pattern): a row of mini lane tiles under the instruction, one arrow glyph per lane in road order, with `valid` lanes highlighted (e.g. green/bold) and unusable lanes dimmed. Combined-indication lanes render a composite arrow, optionally emphasizing the arrow that matches the step's modifier.
2. **Plain-language hints** derived from the valid-lane positions: "use the left 2 lanes", "use the rightmost lane", "any lane" — computed from where the `valid: true` run sits within the array.
3. **Lane-count context on keep/fork steps**: "3 lanes — keep left" pairs naturally with the offset keep-arrows we just added, telling the driver both the direction *and* which lanes get them there.
4. **The same mini strip in the maneuver-marker popups** on the map, so hovering a dot shows the lane setup at that point.

Two design decisions to make if you want this built: *which* intersection's lanes to show per step (convention is the approach to the maneuver — the last lane-bearing intersection before the maneuver point — since a step can traverse several lane-bearing intersections, as the Willow Ave example shows), and whether to render arrows as unicode glyphs (matching the current maneuver icons, zero assets) or small SVGs (crisper composites for multi-indication lanes).

Want me to implement the lane strip in the list?

/**
 * Helpers for the draggable route-vertex handles.
 */

export interface VertexProps {
  /** Index of the vertex in the route geometry. */
  idx: number;
  /** Lowest integer zoom at which the handle is shown (thinning). */
  minzoom: number;
}

export type VertexCollection = GeoJSON.FeatureCollection<GeoJSON.Point, VertexProps>;

const EARTH_RADIUS_M = 6371008.8;
/** Minimum on-screen spacing between neighbouring handles, in CSS px. */
const MIN_SPACING_PX = 28;
const MIN_ZOOM = 4;
const MAX_ZOOM = 20;
/** Sentinel for vertices too dense to show at any zoom. */
const NEVER = 99;

function haversineM(a: number[], b: number[]): number {
  const toRad = Math.PI / 180;
  const dLat = (b[1] - a[1]) * toRad;
  const dLng = (b[0] - a[0]) * toRad;
  const s =
    Math.sin(dLat / 2) ** 2 +
    Math.cos(a[1] * toRad) * Math.cos(b[1] * toRad) * Math.sin(dLng / 2) ** 2;
  return 2 * EARTH_RADIUS_M * Math.asin(Math.sqrt(s));
}

/** Ground resolution for a 512px-tile scheme (maplibre) at a given zoom. */
function metersPerPixel(zoom: number, lat: number): number {
  return (78271.517 * Math.cos((lat * Math.PI) / 180)) / 2 ** zoom;
}

/**
 * Builds one point feature per interior route vertex. Each carries a
 * `minzoom` so a zoom filter can keep handles at least ~28px apart:
 * handles kept at lower zooms stay kept at higher zooms, and new ones are
 * added only where they fit between existing neighbours.
 */
export function buildVertexFeatures(coords: number[][]): VertexCollection {
  const n = coords.length;
  const features: VertexCollection['features'] = [];
  if (n < 3) return { type: 'FeatureCollection', features };

  // Cumulative distance along the route
  const cum = new Float64Array(n);
  for (let i = 1; i < n; i++) cum[i] = cum[i - 1] + haversineM(coords[i - 1], coords[i]);

  const midLat = coords[Math.floor(n / 2)][1];
  const minzoom = new Array<number>(n).fill(NEVER);
  // Endpoints act as anchors for spacing but are never handles (they are
  // the origin/destination markers)
  let kept: number[] = [0, n - 1];

  for (let z = MIN_ZOOM; z <= MAX_ZOOM; z++) {
    const spacing = MIN_SPACING_PX * metersPerPixel(z, midLat);
    const next: number[] = [];
    for (let k = 0; k < kept.length - 1; k++) {
      const a = kept[k];
      const b = kept[k + 1];
      next.push(a);
      let last = cum[a];
      for (let i = a + 1; i < b; i++) {
        if (cum[i] - last >= spacing && cum[b] - cum[i] >= spacing) {
          minzoom[i] = z;
          next.push(i);
          last = cum[i];
        }
      }
    }
    next.push(n - 1);
    kept = next;
  }

  for (let i = 1; i < n - 1; i++) {
    if (minzoom[i] === NEVER) continue;
    features.push({
      type: 'Feature',
      id: i,
      properties: { idx: i, minzoom: minzoom[i] },
      geometry: { type: 'Point', coordinates: [coords[i][0], coords[i][1]] },
    });
  }
  return { type: 'FeatureCollection', features };
}

/** Index of the route vertex closest to a point (planar, lat-corrected). */
export function nearestVertexIndex(coords: number[][], point: [number, number]): number {
  const kx = Math.cos((point[1] * Math.PI) / 180);
  let best = 0;
  let bestD = Infinity;
  for (let i = 0; i < coords.length; i++) {
    const dx = (coords[i][0] - point[0]) * kx;
    const dy = coords[i][1] - point[1];
    const d = dx * dx + dy * dy;
    if (d < bestD) {
      bestD = d;
      best = i;
    }
  }
  return best;
}

/**
 * Position in the intermediate-waypoint list for a waypoint created from
 * route vertex `vertexIdx`: after every existing waypoint the route reaches
 * before that vertex.
 */
export function waypointInsertIndex(
  coords: number[][],
  intermediates: [number, number][],
  vertexIdx: number
): number {
  let index = 0;
  for (const wp of intermediates) {
    if (nearestVertexIndex(coords, wp) < vertexIdx) index++;
  }
  return index;
}

/**
 * Route Vertices — hover the route polyline to reveal its vertices, then
 * drag one off the line to insert an intermediate waypoint at that point
 * in the route sequence.
 */
'use client';

import React, { useEffect, useMemo, useRef, useState } from 'react';
import { Source, Layer, Marker, useMap } from 'react-map-gl';
import type { CircleLayer } from 'react-map-gl';
import type {
  Map as MaplibreMap,
  MapMouseEvent,
  MapGeoJSONFeature,
} from 'maplibre-gl';
import { Box } from '@mui/material';
import { useAppDispatch, useAppSelector } from '@/store/hooks';
import { buildVertexFeatures, waypointInsertIndex } from '@/utils/routeVertices';

/** Wide, invisible copy of the route used as the hover target. */
export const ROUTE_HIT_LAYER_ID = 'route-hit';
const SOURCE_ID = 'route-vertices-source';
const VERTEX_LAYER_ID = 'route-vertices';
/** Half-size of the pick box around the cursor for vertex hits, in px. */
const PICK_PX = 7;
/** Grace period before hiding handles once the cursor leaves the line. */
const HIDE_DELAY_MS = 250;

interface RouteVerticesProps {
  geometry: GeoJSON.LineString;
  /**
   * Set to true when a vertex drag completes so the map's click handler
   * ignores the click maplibre fires on mouseup.
   */
  suppressClickRef: React.MutableRefObject<boolean>;
}

interface DragState {
  idx: number;
  lngLat: [number, number];
}

const vertexLayerStyle: CircleLayer = {
  id: VERTEX_LAYER_ID,
  type: 'circle',
  source: SOURCE_ID,
  // Thin handles so neighbours stay ~28px apart at the tile's zoom
  filter: ['<=', ['get', 'minzoom'], ['zoom']],
  paint: {
    'circle-radius': ['interpolate', ['linear'], ['zoom'], 8, 3.5, 14, 5, 18, 6.5],
    'circle-color': [
      'case',
      ['boolean', ['feature-state', 'hover'], false],
      '#1976D2',
      '#ffffff',
    ],
    'circle-stroke-color': '#1976D2',
    'circle-stroke-width': 2,
    'circle-pitch-alignment': 'map',
  },
};

export const RouteVertices: React.FC<RouteVerticesProps> = ({
  geometry,
  suppressClickRef,
}) => {
  const { current: mapRef } = useMap();
  const dispatch = useAppDispatch();
  const intermediates = useAppSelector((state) => state.waypoints.intermediates);

  const [hovered, setHovered] = useState(false);
  const [drag, setDrag] = useState<DragState | null>(null);

  latest.current = { coords: geometry.coordinates, intermediates, dispatch, suppressClickRef };

  useEffect(() => {
    const map = mapRef?.getMap() as unknown as MaplibreMap | undefined;
    if (!map) return;
    const canvas = map.getCanvas();

    let hideTimer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null = null;
    let hoverId: number | null = null;
    let dragging: DragState | null = null;
    let savedCursor: string | null = null;

    const setCursor = (cursor: string) => {
      if (savedCursor === null) savedCursor = canvas.style.cursor;
      canvas.style.cursor = cursor;
    };
    const resetCursor = () => {
      if (savedCursor !== null) {
        canvas.style.cursor = savedCursor;
        savedCursor = null;
      }
    };

    const show = () => {
      if (hideTimer) {
        clearTimeout(hideTimer);
        hideTimer = null;
      }
      setHovered(true);
    };
    const scheduleHide = () => {
      if (hideTimer) return;
      hideTimer = setTimeout(() => {
        hideTimer = null;
        if (!dragging) setHovered(false);
      }, HIDE_DELAY_MS);
    };

    const setHoverState = (id: number | null) => {
      if (hoverId === id) return;
      if (hoverId !== null && map.getSource(SOURCE_ID)) {
        map.setFeatureState({ source: SOURCE_ID, id: hoverId }, { hover: false });
      }
      if (id !== null && map.getSource(SOURCE_ID)) {
        map.setFeatureState({ source: SOURCE_ID, id }, { hover: true });
      }
      hoverId = id;
    };

    const existing = (ids: string[]) => ids.filter((id) => map.getLayer(id));

    const vertexAt = (point: { x: number; y: number }): MapGeoJSONFeature | undefined => {

      if (!layers.length) return undefined;
      const feats = map.queryRenderedFeatures(

      map.off('mouseup', onMouseUp);
      window.removeEventListener('mouseup', onWindowMouseUp);
      resetCursor();
      setHoverState(null);
      setDrag(null);
      setHovered(false);

      const { coords, intermediates, dispatch, suppressClickRef } = latest.current;
      suppressClickRef.current = true;
      dispatch.waypoints.addWaypoint({
        coordinates: lngLat,
        index: waypointInsertIndex(
          coords,
          intermediates.map((wp) => wp.coordinates),
          idx
        ),
      });
    };

    const onMouseMove = (e: MapMouseEvent) => {
      if (dragging) {
        dragging = { idx: dragging.idx, lngLat: [e.lngLat.lng, e.lngLat.lat] };
        setDrag(dragging);
        return;
      }
      const vertex = vertexAt(e.point);
      if (vertex) {
        show();
        setHoverState(typeof vertex.id === 'number' ? vertex.id : null);
        setCursor('grab');
        return;
      }
      setHoverState(null);
      resetCursor();
      if (onLine(e.point)) show();
      else scheduleHide();
    };

    const onMouseUp = (e: MapMouseEvent) => finish([e.lngLat.lng, e.lngLat.lat]);
    const onWindowMouseUp = () => {
      if (dragging) finish(dragging.lngLat);
    };

    const onMouseDown = (e: MapMouseEvent) => {
      if (dragging || e.originalEvent.button !== 0) return;
      const vertex = vertexAt(e.point);
      const idx = vertex?.properties?.idx;
      if (typeof idx !== 'number') return;
      // Keep the map from panning while the handle is dragged
      e.preventDefault();
      dragging = { idx, lngLat: [e.lngLat.lng, e.lngLat.lat] };
      setDrag(dragging);
      setCursor('grabbing');
      map.on('mouseup', onMouseUp);
      window.addEventListener('mouseup', onWindowMouseUp);
    };

    const onMouseOut = () => {
      if (dragging) return;
      setHoverState(null);
      resetCursor();
      scheduleHide();
    };

    map.on('mousemove', onMouseMove);
    map.on('mousedown', onMouseDown);
    map.on('mouseout', onMouseOut);

    return () => {
      map.off('mousemove', onMouseMove);
      map.off('mousedown', onMouseDown);
      map.off('mouseout', onMouseOut);
      map.off('mouseup', onMouseUp);
      window.removeEventListener('mouseup', onWindowMouseUp);
      if (hideTimer) clearTimeout(hideTimer);
      dragging = null;
      resetCursor();
    };
  }, [mapRef]);

  return (
    <>
      <Source id={SOURCE_ID} type="geojson" data={vertices} maxzoom={20}>
        <Layer
          {...vertexLayerStyle}
          layout={{ visibility: hovered || drag ? 'visible' : 'none' }}
        />
      </Source>

      {/* Ghost of the waypoint being created, follows the cursor */}
      {drag && (
        <Marker
          longitude={drag.lngLat[0]}
          latitude={drag.lngLat[1]}
          anchor="center"
          style={{ pointerEvents: 'none' }}
        >
          <Box
            sx={{
              width: 24,
              height: 24,
              borderRadius: '50%',
              bgcolor: '#757575',
              border: '2px solid white',
              boxShadow: '0 2px 6px rgba(0,0,0,0.35)',
              opacity: 0.9,
            }}
          />
        </Marker>
      )}
    </>
  );
};

export default RouteVertices;
EOF
